# Monorepo

This is a [monorepo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monorepo) containing the entire codebase of Purplefish Software Inc.

- Apps & web services are located in `apps`.
- Shared modules and libraries are located in `packages`.

The services and libraries are deployed automatically via GitHub Actions pipelines whenever a new commit is pushed to the **main** branch.

- Package manager: [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/)
- Build system: [Turborepo](https://turbo.build/)
- App frameworks
  - Web services are built with [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/docs/) (App Router)
  - Background tasks are managed with [Inngest](https://www.inngest.com/)
- CSS framework: [Tailwind](https://tailwindcss.com/)
- API frameworks: [Next.js Server Actions](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/server-actions-and-mutations)
- UI components: based on [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/)
- Database: [PostgreSQL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PostgreSQL) hosted on [Neon](https://neon.tech/)
- Icons: [Material Symbols Sharp](https://fonts.google.com/icons)

## Setup

- Setup `nvm`: https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm
- Install Node.js with `nvm`: `nvm install 22`
- Install pnpm: https://pnpm.io/installation
- Install packages: `pnpm install`

For development, we recommend using either [Cursor](https://www.cursor.com/) or [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/). Once installed, make sure to install all the recommended extensions. When you open a workspace for the first time, the editor will prompt you to install them automatically. You can also manually review the list by running the **Extensions: Show Recommended Extensions** command. Recommended extensions are specified in `.vscode/extensions.json`. Learn more about workspace-recommended extensions [here](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/extension-marketplace#_workspace-recommended-extensions).

## Local development

While it's possible to connect to the production database locally using `envs/production.env` via 1Password, **this is strongly discouraged**. Instead, follow these steps to set up a local development environment:

1. **Create a local environment file**

   ```sh
   cp envs/development.env envs/.env
   ```
   
   - You can also do this using the vercel CLI, by installing the vercel CLI, then using `vercel link` to link this app, and finally running `vercel env pull` to pull in the latest env vars into an env file. This approach will not set all the required env vars, however, so you will be better served with the above method (i.e: copying the development env vars over)

2. **Create a development branch on Neon**
   - Install the neon cli by using `brew install neonctl`
   - Navigate to `apps/app` and run `npm run db:dev` - this will save your env credentials to `apps/app/.env.local`
   - This script will create a dev branch for your user. This dev branch will contain all production data up to the current moment.
   - You can reset the dev branch at any time to sync with the latest production data and schema by running `npm run db:dev:reset`

3. **Update your database configuration**
   - Running `npm run db:dev` in step 2 (above) creates a new `.env.local` file in the `apps/app` directory.
   - Copy the newly created `apps/app/.env.local` file to the `./env` - this will propagate the DB access credentials to npx

4. **Run the development server**
   ```sh
   op run --env-file="./envs/.env" -- npx turbo dev
   ```
   This ensures the environment variables in `.env` are used.

Following these steps will provide a safe and up-to-date development environment without risking unintended changes to production data.

## Create database migrations

Whenever you make changes to the database schema, you need to create a new migration.

```sh
npx turbo db:migrate-dev -- --name "migration-name"
```

or run `npx prisma migrate dev` in the `packages/db` directory.

This will create a new migration file in the `packages/db/prisma/migrations` directory.

### Removing column(s) from a Prisma schema without downtime

Prisma requires all columns defined in `prisma.schema` to exist in the database. If a column is missing, even if unused, Prisma may throw validation errors.

To safely remove columns without downtime, follow these steps:

1. **Update the Prisma Schema**: Remove the column from `prisma.schema`, then deploy the updated schema along with any services that depend on Prisma to production.
2. **Apply Database Migration**: After ensuring that all deployed services no longer reference the removed column, create and deploy a migration to drop the column(s) from the database.

Developers can achieve this by simply creating two separate consecutive pull requests.

## Debug webhooks

To integrate with third-party services, we use webhooks in some cases—for example, LiveKit sends webhook requests to notify us when a call starts or ends.

To test these webhook endpoints, we need to expose them publicly. This requires installing [ngrok](https://ngrok.com) and configuring the third-party service to use the generated ngrok webhook URL.

## Work with Inngest

We use **Inngest** for handling background tasks and event-driven workflows.

1. Start the Inngest Dev Server:

   ```sh
   npx inngest-cli@latest dev -u http://localhost:3000/api/inngest
   ```

   This runs the server at **http://localhost:8288/**.

2. Run Next.js dev server:

   ```sh
   op run --env-file="./envs/.env" -- npx turbo dev --filter=@purplefish-ai/app
   ```

3. Inngest Dev Server will automatically detect and connect to our dev server.

## Upgrade Dependencies

While it is possible to use built-in commands from a package manager (e.g., npm or pnpm) to upgrade dependencies, using [npm-check-updates](https://www.npmjs.com/package/npm-check-updates), a third-party tool, is often a better and more convenient option.

```sh
npm install -g npm-check-updates # Install npm-check-updates globally
ncu --deep # Check for all available dependency updates
ncu --deep --target=minor # Check only for minor updates
ncu --deep -u # Apply all available dependency updates to package.json
ncu --deep --target=minor -u  # Apply available minor dependency updates to package.json
pnpm install # Install new versions and update the lock file
pnpm dedupe # Clean up the lock files and deduplicate dependencies
```

If a new version has compatibility issues and you want to exclude it from `npm-check-updates`, add it to the `reject` array in `.ncurc.json`.

## Common commands

- Run development server: `npx turbo dev`
- Run development server with production environment variables: `op run --env-file="./envs/production.env" -- npx turbo dev`
- Run development server (one project): `npx turbo dev --filter=[PROJECT]` (`PROJECT` is the name (or part of the name) of the project in the `apps` directory, e.g. `app` or `@purplefish-ai/app`)
- Build for production: `npx turbo build`
- Build for production (one project): `npx turbo build --filter=[PROJECT]`
- Format code with Prettier: `npx turbo format`
- Run linter and format checker: `npx turbo lint`
- Run local Inngest server: `npx inngest-cli@latest dev -u http://localhost:5220/api/inngest`
- Run code generation to automatically generate the client for the messaging-agents service: `pnpm run generate-messaging-agents-client`

You can also navigate to a specific project's directory to run it, for example:

```bash
cd apps/app
op run --env-file="./envs/.env" -- npx turbo dev
```

## Automatically Generating the Client for the Messaging Agents Service
The Messaging Agents service uses OpenAPI, so we are able to automatically generate a TypeScript client for it, using
the openapi-ts package. 

To generate the client, run the following command:
```bash
pnpm run generate-messaging-agents-client
```

This will fetch the OpenAPI spec from the messaging-agents service and generate the TypeScript client. The generated 
client must be committed to the repository - by doing so, we make it easier for reviewers to see the changes
made to the API.

## Recent Updates

### Performance Optimizations (August 2025)
- **Fixed infinite state re-rendering in engagement submission logic**: Optimized the side panel engagement flags component by replacing `useEffect` with `useMemo` hooks to prevent unnecessary re-renders when managing engagement flags. This significantly improves UI performance when working with engagement data.
- **Enhanced TRPC provider stability**: Improved the TRPC provider to better handle state changes and prevent cascading re-renders across the application.

## Common commands

- Run development server: `npx turbo dev`
- Run development server with production environment variables: `op run --env-file="./envs/production.env" -- npx turbo dev`
- Run development server (one project): `npx turbo dev --filter=[PROJECT]` (`PROJECT` is the name (or part of the name) of the project in the `apps` directory, e.g. `app` or `@purplefish-ai/app`)
- Build for production: `npx turbo build`
- Build for production (one project): `npx turbo build --filter=[PROJECT]`
- Format code with Prettier: `npx turbo format`
- Run linter and format checker: `npx turbo lint`
- Run local Inngest server: `npx inngest-cli@latest dev -u http://localhost:5220/api/inngest`
- Run code generation to automatically generate the client for the messaging-agents service: `pnpm run generate-messaging-agents-client`
